To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temporal pattern of HCC deaths can be used to estimate the transition probabilities between chronic HCV infection and cirrhosis.

the objective function based on temporal pattern of HCC deaths provides better estimates for the transition probabilities between chronic infection and cirrhosis; and the dynamics of the HCC epidemic is more sensitive to the objective function used than to the model structure or to the data used for the calibration.
a model based on the age at death distribution of HCC deaths can be quite different from a model based on a temporal pattern of HCC deaths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the objective function used to estimate the transition probabilities between chronic and cirrhotic states in a HCV model.
the impact that the choice of objective function has on the estimation of parameters in the HCV model.
the use of the objective function based on temporal pattern of deaths to estimate the transition probabilities in a compartmental model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of objective function is important and should be based on the specific epidemiological question being addressed.

the choice of the objective function used to estimate model parameters is important, and that the temporal pattern of HCC deaths is a better choice than the distribution of the ages at death from HCC.
the choice of objective function is a crucial issue in model building.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the temporal pattern of HCC deaths is more informative than the age‐dependent pattern of HCC death for estimating the transition probabilities between chronic infection and cirrhosis.
the objective function based on HCC deaths by age at death is not a good choice for estimating transition probabilities between chronic and cirrhosis states.
the choice of the objective function is crucial for the determination of the parameters of the model, and the temporal pattern of HCC deaths should be preferred over the distribution of age at death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal pattern of HCC deaths is a much richer source of information than the age distribution of deaths.
the choice of the objective function is critical in the parameter estimation and the subsequent modeling of the epidemic.
the objective function used to estimate model parameters has a significant impact on the dynamics of the model.
